description: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property replaced by BNS Section 318(4)
Punishment for murder replaced by BNS Section 103(1)
Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty replaced by BNS Sections 85 and 86
Information in cognizable cases (FIR) replaced by BNSS Section 173 with explicit provision for Zero FIR and electronic information
Direction for grant of bail to person apprehending arrest (Anticipatory Bail) replaced by BNSS Section 482
Order for maintenance of wives, children and parents replaced by BNSS Section 144
Notice of appearance before police officer in offences punishable up to 7 years replaced by BNSS Section 35(3)
Admissibility of electronic records and mandatory certificate requirement replaced by BSA Section 63

Suraj Lamp (2012) 1 SCC 656 held that General Power of Attorney (GPA), Sale Agreement, or Will transactions do not convey title in immovable property; transfer only via registered conveyance under TPA Section 54 and Registration Act Section 17

metadata.ruling: GPA sales invalid for title transfer

description: Vineeta Sharma (2020) 9 SCC 1 held that daughters have coparcenary rights by birth under Section 6 HSA with effect from birth, irrespective of whether the father was alive on the date of the 2005 amendment

Rajnesh v. Neha (2021) 2 SCC 324 formulated uniform guidelines and made the filing of an Affidavit of Assets and Liabilities mandatory across all maintenance proceedings under BNSS 144, HMA 24, and PWDVA 12

Arnesh Kumar (2014) 8 SCC 273 mandated that police shall not automatically arrest accused in offences punishable with imprisonment up to 7 years without satisfying checklist under Section 41 CrPC (Section 35 BNSS)

metadata.ruling: Notice mandatory prior to arrest for <7 yr offences

description: Lalita Kumari (2014) 2 SCC 1 held that registration of FIR is mandatory under Section 154 CrPC (Section 173 BNSS) if information discloses commission of a cognizable offence

Rangappa v. Sri Mohan (2010) 11 SCC 441 held that presumption under Section 139 NI Act includes the existence of a legally enforceable debt; standard of rebuttal by accused is preponderance of probabilities

metadata.ruling: Reverse burden on drawer in cheque bounce

description: Jitendra Singh (2021) SCC OnLine SC 802 reiterated that mutation of property in revenue records (Khata, RTC, Pahani) does not create or extinguish title; revenue entries are for fiscal taxation purposes only
jurisdiction: Union of India / State of Karnataka

description: Anathula Sudhakar (2008) 4 SCC 594 laid down principles on maintainability of suit for injunction: where plaintiff title is under cloud and he is not in possession, a suit for bare injunction is not maintainable without seeking declaration of title and possession

metadata.ruling: Injunction requires declaration when title disputed

description: Imperia Structures (2020) 10 SCC 783 ruled that remedies under RERA and the Consumer Protection Act are concurrent and alternative; homebuyer is entitled to file consumer complaint despite RERA enactment

metadata.ruling: Consumer Forum and RERA remedies concurrent

description: Danial Latifi (2001) 7 SCC 740 upheld constitutionality of 1986 Act by interpreting that a Muslim husband's obligation to provide fair and reasonable provision and maintenance extends beyond the iddat period for the entire lifetime of the divorced wife

metadata.ruling: Lifetime maintenance for divorced Muslim woman

description: Jacob Mathew (2005) 6 SCC 1 held that to convict a medical professional for criminal negligence under IPC 304A / BNS 106(1), the negligence must be gross, and an independent expert opinion must be obtained before arresting the doctor

Manchegowda (1984) 3 SCC 301 upheld the constitutional validity of the Karnataka PTCL Act, holding that alienation of granted land to SC/ST persons without prior government permission is null and void

Nekkanti Rama Lakshmi (2020) 14 SCC 232 held that where no limitation period is prescribed under Section 5 PTCL Act, application for resumption must be filed within a reasonable time; decades of delay disentitles restoration

metadata.ruling: Reasonable period limitation applies to PTCL

description: Sale deed must be executed and registered to convey legal ownership
Registration is compulsory for all transfers of immovable property valued over Rs 100
Suit for declaration of title and possession under Specific Relief Act
Mutation and RTC entry in Karnataka reflects fiscal possession, but not substantive title
12-year statutory limitation period for recovery of possession based on title
Criminal liability for cheque dishonour for insufficiency of funds
Right of allottee to refund of amount paid with interest, or monthly interest for delayed possession

metadata.forum: Real Estate Regulatory Authority (RERA) / Consumer Commission

description: Application to Magistrate for protection orders, residence order, monetary relief, and custody
Zero customer liability if third-party fraud notified to bank within 3 working days

metadata.forum: Banking Ombudsman / National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal

description: Statutory demand notice must be dispatched in writing within 30 days of receiving cheque return memo from bank
Criminal complaint under Section 138 must be filed within 1 month (30 days) after the 15-day notice period expires

metadata.trigger: Expiry of 15 days from notice receipt

description: Consumer complaint must be filed within 2 years from date on which cause of action arose (extendable only on sufficient cause)

metadata.trigger: Date of deficiency/defect or cause of action

description: Public Information Officer must provide information within 30 days of application (or within 48 hours if concerning life or liberty)
Complaint of sexual harassment must be made to Internal Committee within 3 months of incident (extendable by 3 months for reasons recorded in writing)
Judicial Magistrate First Class (or Metropolitan Magistrate in presidency towns) within whose local jurisdiction the payee bank account is maintained
State Real Estate Regulatory Authority (Karnataka RERA) for refund/interest; Adjudicating Officer for compensation
jurisdiction: State of Karnataka / Union of India

Tahsildar (Form 12 disputed mutation enquiry); First appeal before Assistant Commissioner under Section 136(2) Karnataka Land Revenue Act; Revision before Deputy Commissioner under Section 136(3)
Assistant Commissioner of the Revenue Sub-division under Section 5 PTCL Act; Appeal lies before Deputy Commissioner of the District
Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council (MSEFC) via MSME Samadhaan portal; conciliation followed by binding arbitration
